spans.text: Hey n8n community, if you send your team, your investors or your clients a review deck every month, here’s a free n8n workflow template for business review videos: your report in, a narrated 2 to 4

Import the workflow from the gallery link above, or open a new workflow, click ⋯ → Import from File and pick the attached report-summary-videos.json. Add your Shotstack API key to Make the video and Check the render. You can start a free trial here: Shotstack - The Cloud Video Editing API Add an API key for your AI model to the Claude steps. Claude Opus 5.5 is the model I’ve had the most success with. Fill in Your report: the file name, your company name, your brand colours and who’s watching (the team, the board, clients). Put your file in a reports folder in n8n’s files folder. In Docker, mount a folder from your computer there, for example -v ./n8n-files:/home/node/.n8n-files. On an npm install the folder is .n8n-files in your home folder. Click Execute workflow. A video takes about 15 minutes. What it costs and how long it takes

spans.text: I am building a scenario in Make.com to handle customer messages received through Facebook Messenger. Customers can send either text messages or images. I use a Router to separate incoming messages into two routes: Text route: Processes text messages. Image route: Detects image messages and downloads the images so they can be used later in the scenario. The problem occurs when a customer sends an image along with a message such as, “I want this product.” Even though the image has already been received and downloaded, the AI agent asks the customer to send the image again. I want the AI agent to recognize that the image has already been received and use the available image to identify the product, rather than asking the customer to resend it. How can I structure my Make.com scenario so that both the text and image routes provide the necessary information to the same AI agent, allowing it to understand the customer’s message and analyze the image when one has been provided?
